question: If the difference between the simple interest and compound interest on a sum of money invested for 2 years at the rate of 15% per annum (interest compound annually) is ₹225, then what is the sum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Principle x r²/(100)²

⇒ 225 = P times 15 times 15 over 100 times 100

⇒ P = Rs. 10000

**∴ Sum is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Rs. 225

Rate of interest (R) = 15% per annum

Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (P x R x T)/100, and

Compound Interest = [P (1 + R/100)T- P]

Where P = Principle or Sum

R = Rate of interest per annum

T= Time

**Calculation:**

Let Sum = P

⇒ SI = P x 15 x 2/100 = 30P/100

⇒ CI = P (1 + 15/100)² - P

⇒ P (23/20)² - P

⇒ 529P - 400P/400

⇒ 129P/400

According to question,

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years:

⇒ 225 = ​​129P/400 - 30P/100​

⇒ 225 = (129P - 120P)/400

⇒ 225 = 9P/400

⇒ P = Rs. 10000

∴ Sum is Rs. 10000.
